reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a perfectly flat, zero-valued line across all scales, indicating complete absence of variation, trend, curvature, or noise. All four reference candidates exhibit identical morphology: a constant robust-standardized value of exactly 0.0 over their respective intervals (1P, 3P, 3P, and 5P). The period is trivially undefined due to lack of oscillation; cadence is irrelevant as no cycles occur. Stability is maximal—no deviation from baseline at any point. Amplitude is zero (90th percentile amplitude = 0), roughness and curvature are zero, and slope per point is zero. Peaks and troughs are absent; the entire signal is a flat baseline with no morphological features. Noise is undetectable (MAD = 0.0 in all catalog entries), suggesting either perfect stationarity or data that has been artificially flattened (e.g., constant sensor output or post-processing artifact). Acceptable variation is strictly zero: any non-zero deviation—however small—constitutes an anomaly. This extreme simplicity implies the channel represents a static physical quantity or a diagnostic null state. Given the dataset metadata indicates trend-stationarity and non-zero trend coefficients, this flatness likely reflects local normalization residuals rather than raw sensor behavior, but for the purpose of anomaly detection, the consensus normal is unequivocally a zero-flatline.

reference_profiles.description: A 3-point flat line at y=0.0 spanning indices [0,2]; no variation, no slope, no noise; minimal context (1 cycle equivalent) but fully consistent with zero baseline.
A 9-point flat line at y=0.0 over [494,502]; identical to candidate 0 but with triple the duration (3 cycles); confirms zero baseline persists over longer windows without drift or noise.
Another 9-point flat line at y=0.0 over [987,995]; visually indistinguishable from candidate 1; reinforces consensus across different temporal locations in the series.
A 15-point flat line at y=0.0 over [1475,1489]; longest candidate (5 cycles); confirms zero baseline holds over maximum reference window; no onset/offset transients or edge effects.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference candidate 3 (5P) for queries with ≥5 cycles of context, as it provides the most robust validation of sustained flatness. For shorter queries (≤3 cycles), use candidates 1 or 2—they are interchangeable and equally reliable. Candidate 0 is acceptable only for ultra-short (1–2 point) checks but lacks temporal redundancy; avoid using it alone for inference. All references agree perfectly, so no conflict resolution is needed; any deviation from zero in a query should be flagged regardless of reference choice.
uncertainties: Whether the zero-flatline reflects true physical normality or a preprocessing artifact (e.g., median/MAD standardization of a near-constant signal);
If real anomalies are subtle deviations (e.g., ±0.001) below plot resolution, they may be invisible in these plots;
No evidence of expected periodicity (period=3 from metadata) appears in references—suggesting the periodic component may have been removed or is absent in this channel.
